selected_findings.title: Enable nix-command inside the workflow guard
selected_findings.why_it_matters: The ci-workflow-docs-skip derivation fails before checking its matrix contract in a clean Linux build sandbox. The new subprocess uses the experimental nix eval command, but neither its arguments nor the derivation enable nix-command; the invoking developer or Actions runner's Nix configuration is not a declared sandbox input. Explicitly enabling the feature makes this pure expression evaluation independent of host configuration.

evidence: tests/darwin-outputs.nix:105 --   authEffects = pkgs.writeText "containers-auth-effects.py" ''
tests/podman-containers.nix:24 --   authEffects = pkgs.writeText "containers-auth-effects.py" ''

Read and compared both complete authEffects definitions: their 37-line Nix blocks are byte-identical, including the fresh-home, dry-run, exact JSON, file/directory mode, and existing-byte preservation assertions.

tests/darwin-outputs.nix:220-221 extracts stepBlock containersAuth from the materialized generation and executes authEffects; tests/podman-containers.nix:239 executes the same probe over authBlock. These callers preserve distinct platform delivery coverage when the probe is shared.
selected_findings.suggested_fix: Extract the byte-identical authEffects body into tests/lib/containers-auth-effects.py and reference it from both checks, preserving both platform suites and their distinct delivery boundaries.
selected_findings.title: Duplicate containers-auth probe creates parallel maintenance owners
selected_findings.why_it_matters: Changes to the containers-auth lifecycle contract now require editing two byte-identical runtime probes, so a correction to permissions, preservation, or dry-run coverage can leave the other platform testing an older contract. The Linux and Darwin suites exercise distinct delivery boundaries and should remain independent, but their shared probe implementation need not be copied. Extracting the probe preserves both executions while giving the assertions one maintenance owner.

evidence: tests/lib/agent-activation.py:65: `result = subprocess.run([bash, '-e', str(block)], env=current,`
tests/lib/agent-activation.py:56: `env.pop('DRY_RUN', None)`. Live runs are tested with DRY_RUN unset, the same as Home Manager's live runs, where DRY_RUN is only exported for dry runs.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:203: `if [[ -v DRY_RUN ]]; then`. This is the -u-safe form; a refactor to `[ -n "$DRY_RUN" ]` would expand to empty under `bash -e`, take the live branch, and satisfy every call/args/Pi-link/refusal assertion plus the dry-run pass. Under HM's `set -u` the same line aborts activation.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:257-259: 'linkGeneration sits behind these entries in the built activation script, so this position keeps a refusal from stranding installPackages but not from stranding linkGeneration' — so a -u abort here leaves home files unlinked.

Same diff, tests/podman-containers.nix authEffects: `subprocess.run(["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c", ...])`, and tests/vscodium.nix: `${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash -eu "$redirected"`. The shared harness is the weakest of the new execution harnesses.
Locally available pinned Home Manager source modules/home-environment.nix:860-863 sets -eu, pipefail and cd $HOME; reviewed harness line 65 passes only -e.
selected_findings.suggested_fix: Run the block under the same shell options Home Manager's activation script uses: `subprocess.run([bash, '-euo', 'pipefail', str(block)], ...)`. Optionally set cwd=str(home) to match HM's `cd $HOME`. This is the same strictness the sibling harnesses in this diff already use: podman-containers/darwin-outputs authEffects use `-euo pipefail` and vscodium uses `-eu`.
selected_findings.title: Activation harness runs without -u, passing blocks that abort under Home Manager
selected_findings.why_it_matters: This harness is now the only runtime proof for the claude, codex-settings, gemini, tokscale and agent-plugins activation blocks. Home Manager runs activation under `set -eu` and `set -o pipefail`, but the harness runs each block with `bash -e` only. A block that reads an unset variable passes every harness assertion here, then aborts the real `home-manager switch` with an 'unbound variable' error. Per the module's own comment, a failure at that point strands linkGeneration, so the user's declared home files are never linked, while CI stays green.
